page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server is configured with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs, utilizing hyperthreading with 2.0 threads per core. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 14.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a 3686 GB SSD and supports Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the E96-48ads_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. Its memory subsystem achieves a top-tier rating in the Passmark memory score, ranking in the top 10%, although large-block memory read and write bandwidth benchmarks fall within the average range. Multi-threaded decompression and image processing workloads also register in the top 25%. However, large-scale LLM inference tasks, such as text generation with a 70B model, show poor performance, placing in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high density of memory and local SSD storage relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without needing a proportional increase in compute cores. The combination of 672.0 GB of RAM, a 3686 GB local SSD, and strong multi-core performance makes this server suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale caching layers, and data processing pipelines.
